Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the chase! The umpires are out in the middle and South Africa Women after the final pep talk in a huddle are spreading out in the field. Danni Wyatt-Hodge and Maia Bouchier are the openers striding out for England. Marizanne Kapp has the new ball in hand and is raring to go! Away we go..
... THE RUN CHASE ...

A late cameo from Annerie Dercksen helped South Africa cross the 120-run mark, a total no team has yet achieved on this ground in the competition. Despite the tricky surface and a disciplined Proteas bowling attack, England will be confident heading into the chase with their strong batting lineup. However, they’ll need to start well and carefully navigate the slowness of the pitch, knowing this won't be a straightforward pursuit. Chase coming to you in a bit!

Sarah Glenn is down for a quick chat! She says that it was fun to be out there. Adds that they played here in the last game and got accustomed to the conditions. Mentions that Sophie Ecclestone is great off the field with her communication and she knows what to bowl according to the conditions. Ends by saying that they need to do the basics right, play straight and they have taken some learnings from the last game.

With spinners operating from both ends, England Women successfully tightened the screws, stemming the scoring rate and building pressure on Laura Wolvaardt and Anneke Bosch which led to the dismissal of Bosch breaking the 40 runs stand. Although England let a few more opportunities slip, they made sure those misses didn’t come back to haunt them, keeping the scoring well in check. Much like in their previous match, England's spinners worked in tandem, consistently taking wickets and preventing any new batter from settling in. This included the prized scalp of Marizanne Kapp, who was just beginning to look dangerous before England struck again.

After winning the toss and choosing to bat first, Laura Wolvaardt and Tazmin Brits got off to a good start, scoring at a brisk pace. A few fielding lapses from England allowed the opening partnership to flourish. However, in a bid to capitalize on the final over of the Powerplay, South Africa Women lost Tazmin, with Linsey Smith delivering the crucial breakthrough England had been seeking.

A quickfire 20 off 11 from Annerie Dercksen towards the end helped South Africa Women push their total to 124/6, but England Women will be pleased with how they fought back. After it initially looked like South Africa were on track for a much bigger score, England’s disciplined bowling turned the tide, keeping the total within reach.

A dot to end the innings then! 10 runs off the last over! Nat Sciver-Brunt bowls a back-of-the-hand slower one, back of a length, outside off, Annerie Dercksen looks to cut it away but misses. South Africa Women finishes on 124/6!

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match formalities! We can see the England Women in a huddle near the boundary ropes and then they spread out to take their respective field positions. Laura Wolvaardt and Tazmin Brits are the two openers for South Africa Women. Nat Sciver-Brunt has the new ball in her hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

Not far away from the start of this blockbuster clash in Group B but before that, players from both sides make their way out to the middle and line up for their respective national anthems. It will be South Africa's first followed by the national anthem of England.

Chloe Tryon is up for a quick chat. She says that the team had plenty of rest and they have had a couple of training sessions at this venue. Adds that heat was a factor in the last game but they managed it well. Tells that they have practiced in the night as well and it is much cooler and the outfield in Sharjah is a bit slow. Mentions that the wicket looks really good and they have to adjust quickly. Says that they have played against England Women a lot and she has also played in the Hundred which is a good thing to know a few things about their players. Ends by saying that Nonkululeko Mlaba has fired at the right time and they will try to keep things simple and do the basics correctly.

PITCH REPORT - Natalie Germanos is down at the centre for the pitch. She starts by saying it's warm and the pitch number 4 is being used. Adds that the straight boundary is 73 meters while the square boundaries are 59 meters and 63 meters which will have to be accounted for. Lisa Sthalekar joins in and says that about 72 percent of the overs in the last 4 matches at this venue have been bowled by spinners and about 70 percent of wickets have fallen to spin which says everything about this surface. Mentions that the batters will need to move around back and forth to negate spin and there are a couple of patches that might produce some variable bounce. Concludes that 135 could be a par score at this surface.

Heather Knight, the captain of England Women says that they would have done the same. Adds bat they bowled well in the last game and will have to do the same to set the tone. Mentions that batting wasn't easy on this track and there had been a few conversations about how to adjust to the conditions. Says that history does not play a part between the two sides as it is a different day and different conditions as well. Informs they are unchanged too.

Laura Wolvaardt, the skipper of South Africa Women says the surface looks to be a bit slower and they want to add some runs and try to defend. Adds that this is a massive game and they want to improve and look to be perfect. Concludes that they go unchanged.

Their bowling attack remains a formidable force, with spin expected to take centre stage once again. With both teams equally matched and in good form, this clash promises to be fiercely competitive. Hello and a warm welcome to match 9 of the 2024 ICC Women's T20 World Cup, coming to you from the iconic Sharjah Cricket Stadium! We have a high-stakes showdown between two teams brimming with confidence and momentum, England Women face off against South Africa Women! The stage is set, and excitement is mounting as we gear up for what promises to be a pulsating contest between two top-tier sides.
... MATCH DAY ...

A new week in the 9th edition of the ICC Women's T20 World Cup will kick off with a highly anticipated Group B clash between England and South Africa at the iconic Sharjah Cricket Stadium. Both teams come into this game with momentum, having secured wins in their opening encounters. The stakes are high, as whichever side triumphs here will inch closer to securing a semifinal spot. South Africa, the 2023 runners-up have made an emphatic start to their campaign with a dominant win against the West Indies in Dubai. However, they now face a different challenge in Sharjah, where the conditions have been slower and more conducive to spin. Nonkululeko Mlaba, who was instrumental with the ball in their first game, will once again be key on this surface. Her control and ability to extract turn could be pivotal in stifling England’s batting unit. Laura Wolvaardt, Marizanne Kapp, and Sune Luus form the crux of the Proteas' batting unit and will be crucial to their side's success, especially against England’s potent spin attack. With the conditions in mind, the South African think tank might even contemplate adding leggie Seshnie Naidu to bolster their spin resources. On the flip side, England’s campaign got off to a more challenging start. After a steady Powerplay, their batting faltered, and they found themselves defending a modest total of 118 against Bangladesh. However, their spin-heavy bowling attack, led by Linsey Smith, turned the game in their favour, showcasing their ability to adapt to tricky conditions. Danni Wyatt-Hodge was the standout performer with the bat, but England will need more contributions from others, particularly from Nat Sciver-Brunt, Alice Capsey, and captain Heather Knight, who all struggled in their first outing. England’s strength lies in their well-rounded spin attack. With Linsey Smith, Sophie Ecclestone, Charlie Dean and Sarah Glenn all capable of exploiting the Sharjah conditions, they are unlikely to change their bowling combination. Sciver-Brunt and Dani Gibson will provide the medium-pace options, adding balance to their attack. With the tournament heating up, this clash could define the group dynamics, and both teams will be eager to make a statement. Expect a gripping contest as these two strong sides vie for early control in their quest for a semifinal spot. Who are you backing to come out on top?
